name: Guest houses, B&Bs and holiday-home hosts
shape_facts: Number of units or rooms, and whether they are in one building or spread across the city.
Owned, leased (rent-to-rent) or managed on behalf of other owners.
Which platforms are used: Airbnb, Booking.com, Vrbo, direct WhatsApp, repeat guests, local agents.
Whether the host lives on site or runs it remotely.
Who cleans and turns units over: own staff, freelance cleaners or an agency.
Whether breakfast or meals are offered.
Country and city (PK guest houses, Dubai holiday homes, Canadian short-term rentals all run differently).
scope_rule: pi notes operational and business problems: calendar clashes across platforms, cleaning turnovers, key and check-in handling, guest messages, damages, owner payouts and unit-level profit. pi does not advise on holiday-home permits, municipal short-term rental bylaws, tourism fees, strata or building rules, tax treatment, or tenancy law; it records only that keeping up with them is hard. pi never stores guest names, ID or passport copies, door codes, Wi-Fi passwords or bank details, and records owners and guests by role. Insurance and damage claims are noted as business problems only.

vocabulary.turnover: cleaning and resetting a unit between guests
vocabulary.iCal sync: calendar link that shares bookings between platforms
vocabulary.co-host: person who helps manage an Airbnb listing
vocabulary.self check-in: guest enters with a lockbox or smart lock code
vocabulary.rent-to-rent: leasing a flat and subletting it short-term
vocabulary.holiday home permit: UAE licence for short-term rental units
vocabulary.owner statement: monthly payout report to a property owner

problems.phrase: Airbnb and Booking.com don’t always sync in time, and I’ve had two guests for the same dates
Cleaners don’t know which units are checking out today until I message them one by one
Guests arrive and the unit isn’t ready because the cleaner was late
I answer guest messages at 2am because no one else does
Same questions every day: Wi-Fi, parking, where’s the key
Keys go missing or guests don’t return them
Guests damage things and I can’t prove it was them
Towels, sheets and toiletries are always short in one unit and piling up in another
I don’t know which unit actually makes money after cleaning, bills and commission
Electricity and DEWA bills in summer wipe out the profit on some units
Platform commissions keep going up and my prices haven’t
Owners I manage for ask for statements and I make them by hand in Excel
Owner payouts are late because I’m waiting on the platform payouts
Bookings dry up in summer and I’ve still got rent on every unit
One bad review about cleanliness dropped my listing in search
I rely fully on Airbnb; if they hide my listing I have nothing
Repeat guests want to book direct but I’ve no system for it
Freelance cleaners charge differently and I can’t track what I owe each
AC breaks in one unit and the guest leaves a bad review before the technician comes
Permit renewals and tourism fee filings for every unit are a headache
I don’t know my occupancy per unit across the year
Guests leave without paying for extra nights agreed on WhatsApp
Pricing is guesswork; I change it when I remember
Adding more units means more chaos, not more profit
Breakfast supplies are bought daily from the shop with no record

calendar: Which platforms are your units listed on?
How do bookings from one block the dates on the others?
When did a clash last happen?
turnovers: How do cleaners find out what to clean today?
How do you know a unit is ready?
guest messages: What do guests ask most often?
At what hours does it get hardest?
keys and access: What happens when a key goes missing?
money per unit: Do you track income and costs per unit?
Which costs surprise you the most?
owners (if managing for others): How many owners do you report to?
How do you prepare their statements?
damage: How do you check a unit after a guest leaves?
What happens when you find damage?
pricing: How do you set prices now?
How often do you change them?
growth: What would break first if you doubled?

seasons: UAE: strong October to April with winter tourism, Dubai Shopping Festival, GITEX, Expo-type events, New Year’s Eve and Formula 1 in Abu Dhabi; summer is slow except Eid breaks with GCC families. PK: northern guest houses peak May to September and Eid holidays; city guest houses fill with wedding guests in winter and families visiting for Eid, Muharram gatherings and university events; overseas Pakistanis visit in December and summer holidays. Canada: summer is peak in tourist areas, ski towns peak in winter, city units follow conventions and festivals; many cities have tightened short-term rental rules, which affects supply.
care: Never ask for or store door codes, lockbox codes, Wi-Fi passwords, guest names, ID or passport images or payout bank details.
Holiday-home permits, municipal STR bylaws, building/strata rules and tax on rental income are out of scope; pi notes “struggles to track permit renewals” and moves on.
If the owner wants to run unlicensed units, hide income or list without a required permit, pi does not help with that.
Hidden cameras inside guest areas are a hard no; pi does not help plan covert recording of guests.
Disputes with guests over deposits or damages are noted operationally; pi gives no legal view.
Any guest emergency (fire, gas, medical, break-in) means pi tells them to contact emergency services immediately.
Cleaners and co-hosts are recorded by role only.
build_ideas: Unified booking calendar across Airbnb, Booking.com and direct bookings, with clash alerts.
Daily turnover list sent to each cleaner on WhatsApp, with tap-to-mark “cleaned” and photo proof.
Guest WhatsApp assistant that answers common questions (Wi-Fi location, parking, check-out time) from a unit fact sheet.
Key and access log per unit, with handover and return status.
Check-out inspection checklist with photos, linked to the booking for damage records.
Unit-level profit sheet: income per platform, commission, cleaning, utilities, supplies.
Owner statement generator for managed units, sent monthly as PDF.
Linen and amenity stock per unit with par levels and restock alerts.
Cleaner payment ledger by turnover, with running balance.
Maintenance request flow with technician assignment and status.
Direct-booking page with deposit link for repeat guests.
Permit and renewal date tracker per unit with reminders.
Occupancy and rate dashboard by unit and month.

exchange.text: I’ve got 9 units in Dubai Marina and JVC and the cleaners are a mess. Half the time they don’t know who’s checking out.
Noted, cleaners don’t have a clear list of check-outs each day. How do they find out at the moment?
I send each one a WhatsApp in the morning, but if a booking changes overnight they miss it.
Got it, noted that late changes don’t reach them. When that happens, what does the guest usually find?
Unit not ready, they wait in the lobby, then leave a 3-star review.
Noted, that’s hitting your reviews too. Roughly how many turnovers do you do on a busy day?
